newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 14.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 14.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

DUESSELDORF - Euro RSCG ad agency in Duesseldorf plans to double its turnover by the end of 1999, says Chief Executive Gerhard Schoeps. Schoeps says Euro RSCG, which is based in Paris, is in negotiations for an acquisition in a specialised advertising niche in Germany.

CHICAGO - Midas International Corp, the world's largest franchised automotive service operation, shortlists four Chicago agencies to make presentations in its search for a national advertising agency to succeed J. Walter Thompson USA on the $25 million account.

HAMBURG - Ad group Scholz & Friends plans to expand its business in new media and has created two new executive positions in the field. John Eberstein has taken over the "n.a.s.a." (net activities and screen advertising) post and Serge Tzscheetzsch is new chief of consulting, Scholz & Friends says. N.a.s.a. represents clients including Deutsche Bank, Hagenuk and Reemtsma with their multimedia projects.

CHICAGO - Leap Group Inc says it has been selected to develop a TV, press, radio and poster advertising campaign for the introduction of Korean carmaker Daewoo Motor Co Ltd's new car line scheduled for launch in early 1998.
MEXICO CITY - Mexico has aggressive marketing plans for its coffee and plans to shed its low quality image, the Mexican Coffee Council says.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
LONDON - British Sky Broadcasting Plc is considering buying a stake in Formula One, the international motor racing business expected to float on the UK stockmarket this year, newspapers say.

MUNICH - The chief executive of Bertelsmann AG, Michael Dornemann, says he does not expect the European Union to block a plan by Bertelsmann and the Kirch group to become equal partners in pay TV broadcaster Premiere.
WILMINGTON, Delaware - Seagram Co Ltd and Viacom Inc fire a last legal salvo at each other, leaving the fate of their USA Networks cable-television partnership in the hands of a Delaware judge.

NEW DELHI- While economic reforms over the last six years in India have been good news for many industries, foreign investors are realising that broadcasting is a totally different ball game with a minefield of restrictions, say industry experts.

MUNICH - Soccer's governing body FIFA and the Kirch Group of Germany deny press reports that the media giant is in danger of losing broadcasting rights to the 2002 and 2006 World Cups. Several newspapers had reported that Kirch risked losing the television rights by signing a distribution contract with Prisma Sport & Media, a Swiss marketing agency, because FIFA prohibits third-party deals.
LONDON - Britain's Capital Radio Plc plans to open new Radio Cafes as part of its development into a broader music entertainment company, chief executive David Mansfield says.
SYDNEY - Pay television groups Foxtel and Australis Media Ltd are holding merger talks but it was not known if an announcement will be made this week, industry sources say.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

NEW YORK - Campbell Soup Co is considering shedding "nonstrategic" businesses with $1.4 billion is sales, in a move to focus on volume growth in its core soup, sauces, biscuits and food service lines, The Wall Street Journal says.
CAPE TOWN - The South African clothing and textile industry has entered a cautious recovery phase with its hopes pinned on interest rate cuts and increased access to the U.S. market, it says.
STUTTGART, Germany - German sports car maker Porsche AG says it is holding talks with a number of companies including Volkswagen AG about co-operating on the development of a new off-road vehicle.
LONDON - Britain may raise the age at which people can buy cigarettes to 18 from 16, the Sunday Times reports.
LONDON - Britain is to scrap its annual change in car number plates and will replace the system with a twice-yearly launch of new registrations, the Sunday Times newspaper says.
BELGRADE - The Yugoslav government introduces compulsory tax stamps on all tobacco and alcohol in a bid to stifle illegal trade, Tanjug news agency reports.
DETROIT - Chrysler Corp says it expects its incentive spending to remain at its current level of $1,195 per vehicle during the July and August clearance of 1997 models.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
LONDON - One in five young Britons are so pressured at work that they would be willing to take a pay cut to gain more time with their families or hobbies, a survey carried out by MORI reports.

AMSTERDAM - Call centres, where highly-trained staff deal with consumer telephone queries from around the world, are booming business in the Netherlands because of Dutch language skills and professional flexibility, say industry specialists.

LONDON - What do paraffin stoves, candles, cash, bicycles, tins of food, bottles of water, typewriters, and ladders have in common? None of them depend on computer chips, and all are likely to be in desperate demand after clocks strike midnight on December 31, 1999 and the Millennium computer bug strikes, say industry experts.

BERLIN - Snowploughs take to the sunny streets of Berlin to clear up a carpet of cans, bottles and clothing shed during the giant Love Parade techno music fest -- an event which drew up to one million revellers.

HONG KONG - An Australian hair designer and beauty expert has designs on Asian women -- he wants to change their traditional beauty to an "international" look neither classic Eastern nor Western. His skills are in great demand in Hong Kong and Singapore, say observers.
JERUSALEM - Palestinians in Arab East Jerusalem open a shopping festival to encourage commercial and cultural nightlife in an area suffering under Israeli security measures.

WASHINGTON - If Americans could spend a vacation in any other country in the world and cost was not an issue, their clear favourite would be Australia, according to a poll by Louis Harris and Associates, Inc.
